title: Digital Auditing & Assurance
outcomes: Explain digital audit and auditing digitally.
Understand IT environments, risks and dependencies.
Assess cyber risks and conduct remote audits.

meta.exam_tip: Pair each IT weakness with an ITGC or application control.

concepts.title: Digital audit and auditing digitally
body: A digital audit uses technology across the audit — paperless workflows, data analytics, automated tools — to examine entire populations, increase speed and focus on risk. Auditing digitally refers to auditing an entity whose processes, records and controls are digital, requiring the auditor to understand and test IT systems.

Advantages: wider coverage, real-time or continuous auditing, better anomaly detection, efficiency and documentation. Challenges: data quality and access, cyber security, skills, tool reliability, cost and evidence of data completeness.
Professional skepticism and judgement remain central; tools support but do not replace the auditor.
concepts.analogy: Technology expands what auditors can see — judgement still decides.
concepts.work: Testing 100% of transactions replaces small samples.

concepts.title: Understanding the IT environment and IT risks
body: Understanding the IT environment covers applications, databases, operating systems, networks, IT processes (access, change, operations) and outsourced services.

Risks arising from IT: unauthorised access, unauthorised changes to data or programs, failure to update systems, inappropriate manual intervention, data loss, and reliance on inaccurate system reports. IT general controls (access, change management, operations) support application controls.
The auditor identifies IT dependencies — automated controls, calculations, reports used in the audit, interfaces — and tests related controls or the data itself.
concepts.analogy: Know the systems before trusting their output.
concepts.work: A system-generated ageing report needs testing before relying on it.

concepts.title: Cyber risk and remote audit
body: Cyber risk is the risk of loss from failure or breach of information systems — malware, ransomware, phishing, data theft, denial of service — threatening confidentiality, integrity and availability.

Cyber security frameworks (e.g. identify, protect, detect, respond, recover) guide controls: access management, encryption, patching, monitoring, incident response, backups and awareness training. The auditor considers effects of cyber incidents on statements and going concern.
Remote audits use secure document sharing and video tools; auditors must ensure authenticity of documents, confidentiality, and sufficiency of evidence, sometimes using live observation by video.
concepts.analogy: Cyber incidents are audit risks, not just IT problems.
concepts.work: A ransomware attack may require evaluating data integrity and disclosures.

concepts.title: Emerging technologies and next-generation audit
body: Emerging technologies: data analytics (e.g. ACL, IDEA), artificial intelligence and machine learning for anomaly detection and document reading, robotic process automation for repetitive testing, Internet of Things for real-time asset data, blockchain for tamper-resistant records, and drones for inventory observation.
Control objectives in such environments: accuracy, completeness, authorisation, data integrity and security; auditors must understand how tools and models work and validate their outputs.
Next-generation audit moves toward continuous auditing, full-population testing and predictive insights, requiring new skills and quality controls over tools.
concepts.analogy: New tools, same objectives: reliable evidence.
concepts.work: Drones counting coal stockpiles support inventory observation.

jobs.title: Setting up an analytics-led audit
jobs.situation: A retail client processes 10 million transactions annually on an ERP.
steps: Extract full data and verify completeness.
Run analytics and follow up exceptions.
jobs.takeaway: Reliable data plus tested controls make analytics trustworthy.

viva.q: Distinguish digital audit and auditing digitally.
viva.model: Digital audit uses technology to perform the audit; auditing digitally means auditing an entity whose processes and records are digital.
Unauthorised access, unauthorised program or data changes, inappropriate manual intervention and data loss.

viva.q: What are the stages of a cyber security framework?
viva.model: Identify, protect, detect, respond and recover.

viva.q: Give examples of emerging audit technologies.
viva.model: Data analytics, artificial intelligence, robotic process automation, blockchain, IoT and drones.

viva.q: Why must data completeness be checked before analytics?
viva.model: Because conclusions from analytics are only reliable if the extracted data is complete and accurate.

cases.title: CloudKart Ltd.
cases.case: CloudKart, an e-commerce company, suffered a ransomware attack in February; systems were restored from backups within a week. The audit is performed remotely. Developers have admin access to production. The auditor plans to use AI to read 50,000 vendor invoices.

mcqs.q: The ransomware attack requires the auditor to consider:
mcqs.explain: Cyber risk affects evidence. In practice: test restored data.

mcqs.q: Developers' admin access to production is a weakness in:
mcqs.explain: ITGC failure. In practice: substantive testing increases.
mcqs.topic: Understanding the IT environment and IT risks

mcqs.q: In the remote audit, documents should be:
options: Obtained via secure channels and checked for authenticity
mcqs.explain: Evidence reliability. In practice: live video verification.

mcqs.q: Before relying on the AI tool, the auditor should:
mcqs.explain: Tool reliability. In practice: test a sample manually.
